examples.en: I was humiliated in front of a lot of people.

examples.ko: 온갖 수모를 견디고 끝내 꿈을 이뤘어요.
examples.en: He endured all kinds of humiliation and finally achieved his dream.

examples.ko: 그 일은 그에게 평생 잊을 수 없는 수모였어요.
examples.en: That incident was a humiliation he could never forget.
Despite the humiliation, I kept trying without giving up.

examples.ko: 길에서 받은 수모가 아직도 마음에 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The humiliation I suffered on the street still stays in my mind.

examples.ko: 그는 수모와 가난 속에서도 공부를 놓지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even amid humiliation and poverty, he never gave up studying.

explain: 남에게 깔보이거나 모욕을 당하는 일을 겪는 쪽의 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요. '수모를 당하다', '수모를 겪다', '수모를 견디다'처럼 써요. '모욕'은 가하는 쪽에도 쓰지만 '수모'는 당하는 경험을 말해요.

phrases.example: 그는 어린 시절 많은 수모를 겪었어요.
phrases.en: He went through a lot of humiliation in his childhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모욕적인 일을 경험했다고 담담하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say, in a matter-of-fact way, that one experienced humiliation.

phrases.en: She endured the humiliation and kept working to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참기 힘든 모욕을 참고 버틴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to bear and hold out through hard-to-take humiliation.

phrases.example: 이번 경기에서 지난번의 수모를 씻고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to wipe away last time's humiliation in this match.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이전의 창피한 일을 좋은 결과로 만회한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to make up for an earlier disgrace with a good result.

explain_en: It is used from the viewpoint of the person who is looked down on or insulted. Typical uses are '수모를 당하다', '수모를 겪다' and '수모를 견디다'. '모욕' can describe the one who insults too, but '수모' is about the experience of suffering it.

t90.ax: I was humiliated in front of a lot of people.

en: to be disgusting; to be sickening; to be distasteful

examples.ko: 잘난 척하는 모습이 아니꼬워서 보기 싫어요.
examples.en: His showing off is so irritating that I can't stand to look.
The way that person talks is really obnoxious.

examples.ko: 돈 좀 있다고 자랑하는 게 아니꼽게 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: His bragging about having some money felt sickening.
He looked at me with a snooty expression.
Even though I found it distasteful, I held back.

examples.ko: 상사의 행동이 아니꼬웠지만 아무 말도 안 했어요.
examples.en: My boss's behavior galled me, but I said nothing.

explain: 잘난 척하거나 거만한 모습을 보고 비위가 상할 때 써요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '아니꼬워요', '아니꼬운'으로 바뀌어요. 일상에서는 '재수 없다', '꼴사납다'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 사람들이 그의 잘난 척을 아니꼽게 봐요.
phrases.en: People look at his showing off with distaste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 행동이 마음에 안 들어 좋지 않게 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you view someone's behavior unfavorably.

phrases.en: He looked at me with a sneering expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㅂ' 불규칙 활용형 '아니꼬운'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: The irregular form 아니꼬운 modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.example: 그 사람의 거만한 말투가 아니꼬워서 대답도 안 했어요.
phrases.en: His arrogant tone annoyed me, so I didn't even answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used to give a reason.

explain_en: It is used when someone's showing off or arrogance turns your stomach. It is a ㅂ-irregular word, so it becomes '아니꼬워요' and '아니꼬운'. In casual talk people also say things like '재수 없다' or '꼴사납다'.

en: to be concerned about; to pay attention to

examples.ko: 그는 남들의 시선에 아랑곳하지 않고 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: He sang without caring about other people's stares.

examples.ko: 남이 뭐라고 하든 아랑곳할 필요 없어요.
examples.en: No matter what others say, you don't need to care.

examples.ko: 누가 말려도 아랑곳 안 하는 고집쟁이예요.
examples.en: He's a stubborn person who doesn't pay attention no matter who tries to stop him.

examples.ko: 그는 비난에 아랑곳하지도 않고 자기 길을 갔어요.
examples.en: He didn't even mind the criticism and went his own way.

examples.ko: 아무도 그 소문에 아랑곳하는 사람이 없어요.
examples.en: No one cares about that rumor.

examples.ko: 조금이라도 아랑곳했다면 그런 말은 하지 않았을 거예요.
examples.en: If you had cared even a little, you wouldn't have said such a thing.

explain: '~에 아랑곳하지 않고'처럼 거의 부정 표현과 같이 써요. '신경 쓰지 않다'와 비슷하지만 걱정, 시선, 방해가 있어도 흔들리지 않고 계속한다는 느낌이 있어요. 조사는 '에'를 써요.

phrases.example: 아이는 비가 오는 것에 아랑곳하지 않고 놀았어요.
phrases.en: The child kept playing, paying no attention to the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요. '~에 아랑곳하지 않고' 뒤에 계속하는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic usage; the action that continues follows '~에 아랑곳하지 않고'.

phrases.example: 그는 주변 사람들 눈에 아랑곳없이 크게 웃었어요.
phrases.en: He laughed loudly, regardless of the people around him.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아랑곳하지 않고'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 조금 더 짧고 글에서 많이 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '아랑곳하지 않고' but shorter and more common in writing.

phrases.example: 남들이 뭐라고 해도 신경 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.en: I don't mind what others say.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '아랑곳하지 않다' 대신 쓰기 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday alternative to 아랑곳하지 않다.
phrases.en_equiv: to not mind; to not worry about

explain_en: It is almost always used with a negative, as in '~에 아랑곳하지 않고'. It is like '신경 쓰지 않다' (not care), but suggests carrying on without being shaken by worry, stares or interruptions. It takes the particle '에'.

examples.en: He holds a grudge against me.
Out of spite, I deliberately pretended not to know.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 앙심이 깊어서 오래 기억해요.
examples.en: That person holds deep grudges and remembers things for a long time.
The look in his eyes, full of spite, was scary.
If you're consumed by spite, you can't do anything.

examples.ko: 해고된 직원이 앙심을 품고 거짓 소문을 냈어요.
examples.en: The fired employee spread false rumors out of spite.

explain: 상대에게 당한 일 때문에 마음속에 남은 미운 마음이고, 되갚아 주고 싶은 생각까지 담겨 있어요. 보통 '앙심을 품다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람이 앙심을 먹고 복수하려 해요.
phrases.en: That person is nursing a grudge and wants revenge.
phrases.nuance_ko: '앙심을 품다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 더 입말 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 'to harbor a grudge' but more colloquial.

phrases.example: 그의 앙심이 깊어서 쉽게 풀리지 않아요.
phrases.en: His grudge is deep, so it doesn't ease easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미운 마음이 오래 남아 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when resentment lingers for a long time.

phrases.en: We let go of the long grudge and made up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미운 마음을 없앤다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting rid of the resentment.
phrases.en_equiv: to let go of a grudge

explain_en: It is the resentment that stays in your heart because of something someone did to you, often with a wish to get back at them. People usually say '앙심을 품다'.

t90.ax: He holds a grudge against me.

examples.ko: 심판이 오프사이드를 오판해서 팬들이 화가 났어요.
examples.en: The referee misjudged an offside call and the fans got angry.

examples.ko: 상황을 오판하면 큰 손해를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you misjudge the situation, you can suffer a big loss.
I misjudged that person's character.

examples.ko: 날씨를 오판하고 우산 없이 나갔다가 비를 맞았어요.
examples.en: I misjudged the weather, went out without an umbrella and got rained on.

examples.ko: 서두르다가 시장 상황을 오판하지 않도록 조심해요.
examples.en: Be careful not to misjudge the market by rushing.
With so little information, I couldn't help but misjudge.

explain: 심판, 정부, 투자처럼 비교적 중요한 판단이 틀렸을 때 써요. 가벼운 일이라면 '잘못 보다', '착각하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 명사 '오판'으로 '오판이다/오판을 하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 감독이 경기 흐름을 보고 오판을 했어요.
phrases.en: The coach misjudged the flow of the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '오판'에 '하다'를 붙여서 '오판하다'와 같은 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun 오판 plus 하다, meaning the same as 오판하다.

phrases.en: Giving up now is a misjudgment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 결정이 틀렸다고 평가할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to evaluate a decision as mistaken.

phrases.en: I misjudged the situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오판하다'보다 부드럽고 일상 대화에서 쓰기 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 오판하다 and easier to use in daily conversation.

explain_en: It is used when a fairly important judgment, such as a referee's call, a government decision or an investment, turns out wrong. For minor matters '잘못 보다' or '착각하다' sounds more natural. The noun '오판' also works, as in '오판이다/오판을 하다'.

examples.en: My friend cheered me on, so I got a big boost of courage.
Hearing the teacher's praise gave me courage, so I gave my presentation.
The players are filled with courage by the fans' applause.
When my family is next to me, I automatically feel brave.
The child, full of courage, went on the errand alone.

examples.ko: 엄마 말씀을 듣고 용기백배한 얼굴로 시험장에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: After hearing my mom's words, I went into the exam room looking full of courage.

explain: 보통 말할 때는 '용기가 나다', '힘이 나다'라고 해요. '용기백배'는 응원이나 칭찬을 받고 힘이 확 솟을 때 쓰고, 글이나 기사에서 더 자주 보여요. '용기백배해서', '용기백배한 얼굴'처럼 이어서 써요.

phrases.en: He went up on stage with an emboldened look on his face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 솟은 사람의 표정을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the look of someone filled with courage.

phrases.en: Hearing my friend's words gave me courage.
phrases.nuance_ko: '용기백배하다'보다 말할 때 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural in speech than 'yonggibaekbae-hada'.

phrases.en: I get energy when I'm cheered on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기운이 생길 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy expression for when you feel energized.

explain_en: In everyday talk people usually say '용기가 나다' or '힘이 나다'. '용기백배' is used when cheering or praise suddenly gives you strength, and it shows up more in writing and news. It is typically used as '용기백배해서' or '용기백배한 얼굴'.

t90.ax: The child, full of courage, went on the errand alone.

en: to be rather regrettable; to be rather unsatisfactory

examples.en: I'm truly sorry the result turned out this way.
Unfortunately, I can't make it to this gathering.
I have some unfortunate news to share.
Unfortunately, the tickets are all sold out.

examples.ko: 그 일이 일어난 것이 아주 유감스러웠어요.
examples.en: It was very regrettable that it happened.
He said it was regrettable that the promise wasn't kept.

explain: 서운하고 아쉬운 마음을 공손하게 말할 때 써요. '아쉽다'보다 격식 있어서 거절이나 안 좋은 소식을 전할 때 자주 나와요. '유감이다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 쓰고, 친구와는 '아쉽다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 그런 일이 생겨서 정말 유감스러운 일이에요.
phrases.en: It's really a regrettable thing that this happened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사를 명사 앞에 붙여 아쉽고 안타까운 일을 공손하게 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective before a noun politely refers to a regrettable matter.

phrases.en: Unfortunately, today's class was cancelled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안 좋은 소식을 공손하게 시작할 때 문장 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed at the start of a sentence to politely introduce bad news.

phrases.en: I'm really sorry to hear that news.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유감스럽다'보다 짧고 말하기 쉬워서 인사말이나 위로할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter and easier to say than '유감스럽다', often used in condolences.

explain_en: It politely expresses disappointment or regret. It is more formal than '아쉽다', so it often appears when declining or delivering bad news. '유감이다' is used just as often, and with friends '아쉽다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: After getting praised, he puffed up his shoulders proudly.
My younger sibling is swaggering after getting first place on the exam.
He walked proudly in his new shoes.
If you show off too much, your friends won't like it.
It was cute how he swelled with pride at a single compliment.

examples.ko: 상을 받았다고 그렇게 으쓱거릴 것까지는 없어요.
examples.en: You don't need to swagger like that just because you won a prize.

explain: 우쭐해서 뽐내듯 어깨를 들썩이는 모습에 써요. 모르겠다는 뜻으로 어깨를 올리는 동작은 보통 '어깨를 으쓱하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: He shrugged his shoulders as if to say he didn't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모르겠다'는 뜻으로 어깨를 올리는 동작에는 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural for the shoulder shrug that means 'I don't know'.

phrases.en: After the praise, I felt proud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칭찬을 받아서 기분이 좋아지고 뿌듯할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when praise makes you feel good and proud.

phrases.en: My friend has been showing off since winning an award.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이지만 잘난 척하는 느낌이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, with a clearer sense of showing off.

explain_en: It describes swaggering with your shoulders raised out of pride. The gesture of raising your shoulders to say 'I don't know' is usually '어깨를 으쓱하다'.

t90.ax: He walked proudly in his new shoes.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어진 뒤로 계속 의기소침해 있어요.
examples.en: I've been feeling down ever since I failed the exam.
Why do you look so down today?
One word from my friend left me discouraged.

examples.ko: 너무 의기소침하지 말고 다시 한번 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't be too discouraged, try one more time.

examples.ko: 발표를 망쳐서 하루 종일 의기소침한 얼굴이었어요.
examples.en: I messed up my presentation and looked dejected all day.

examples.ko: 아이가 의기소침할 때는 따뜻하게 안아 주세요.
examples.en: When your child is feeling down, give them a warm hug.

explain: '우울하다'보다 가벼운 말로, 실패하거나 지적을 받아서 자신감이 떨어지고 기운이 없을 때 써요. 반대말은 '의기양양하다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '기가 죽다'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: With your shoulders drooping, you look downcast today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'로 겉으로 기운이 없어 보인다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-아/어 보이다' it says someone looks low in spirits.

phrases.en: He came home with a dejected face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 자신감 없는 표정을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a noun to show a face lacking confidence.

phrases.en: I lost heart after being scolded by my senior.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '의기소침하다' 대신 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday alternative to '의기소침하다'.

explain_en: It is lighter than '우울하다' (gloomy) and is used when you lose confidence and energy after a failure or criticism. Its opposite is '의기양양하다'. In everyday talk people also often say '기가 죽다'.

t90.ax: Why do you look so down today?

en: to be now glad, now sad; to have joy and sorrow in alternation

examples.en: Don't swing between joy and sorrow over small things.
I get happy and sad every time my score goes up and down.
I tend to get carried away by the stock price.
I won't get worked up until the results come out.
My parents don't get emotional over my grades.

examples.ko: 친구는 연애 문제로 하루에도 몇 번씩 일희일비해요.
examples.en: My friend's mood swings several times a day over love troubles.

explain: 'N에 일희일비하다' 형태로 써요. 조언할 때는 '일희일비하지 마세요'처럼 부정형으로 많이 말해요. 기쁨과 슬픔이 번갈아 온다는 느낌이라, 계속 좋거나 계속 나쁜 상황에는 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.en: It's better not to swing with every move in the stock price.
phrases.nuance_ko: 충고나 다짐에서 가장 많이 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form most common in advice and resolutions.
phrases.en_equiv: not to be swayed by every change

phrases.en: It was sad to see him swing with every result.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일희일비하는 + 명사' 형태로 사람의 태도를 묘사해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as '일희일비하는 + noun' to describe a person's attitude.

phrases.example: 한 번의 실수에 일희일비할 필요 없어요.
phrases.en: You don't need to get worked up over a single mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 위로하며 마음을 편하게 해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to comfort someone and put them at ease.
phrases.en_equiv: no need to get worked up

explain_en: It is used as 'N에 일희일비하다'. When giving advice people often use the negative, '일희일비하지 마세요'. It implies joy and sadness alternating, so it doesn't fit a situation that is just constantly good or constantly bad.

examples.ko: 계속 실패하자 그는 자포자기 상태가 됐어요.
examples.en: After failing again and again, he fell into a state of despair.
When you fall into despair, you don't feel like doing anything.
It is too early to give up on yourself.
Everyone was surprised by his I-don't-care answer.
I walked into the exam room with a hopeless feeling.
However hard it is, please don't just give up on yourself.

explain: '포기'는 어떤 일을 그만두는 것이고, '자포자기'는 절망해서 자신까지 내던진 듯 아무렇게나 하는 상태예요. '자포자기 상태, 자포자기식 태도'처럼 쓰고 동사는 '자포자기하다'예요.

phrases.en: After failing the exam, I felt like giving up on everything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 절망해서 다 포기하고 싶은 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the feeling of despair when one wants to give up on everything.

phrases.en: If you work in a devil-may-care way, the results get even worse.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-식'을 붙여 아무렇게나 해 버리는 방식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -식, describes a careless, nothing-matters way of doing things.

phrases.example: 그는 요즘 모든 걸 자포자기하고 있어요.
phrases.en: These days he has given up on everything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 표제어에 '-하다'를 붙인 동사로, 행동으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form made with -하다, used when talking about the action.

explain_en: '포기' is quitting a particular thing, while '자포자기' is a state of despair where you stop caring about yourself and do things carelessly. It appears as '자포자기 상태' or '자포자기식 태도', and the verb is '자포자기하다'.

examples.en: This time I made up my mind and started a diet.

examples.ko: 그는 작심한 듯 모든 사실을 털어놓았어요.
examples.en: He seemed to have made up his mind and told everything.

examples.ko: 오늘은 작심해서 방 청소를 끝까지 했어요.
examples.en: Today I was determined and finished cleaning the room to the end.

examples.ko: 작심하면 못 할 일이 없다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think there is nothing you can't do once you set your mind to it.
I've made up my mind, so this time I'll see it through.

examples.ko: 선생님이 작심하셨는지 숙제를 아주 많이 내 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher must have made up their mind, since they gave a lot of homework.

explain: '마음먹다'보다 단단히 각오한 느낌이 있고, 주로 '작심하고 + 동사' 모양으로 써요. '작심한 듯'은 마음먹고 하는 말이나 행동을 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 작심하고 제 생각을 솔직하게 말했어요.
phrases.en: Today I made up my mind and told them my thoughts honestly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참았던 말을 단단히 마음먹고 할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when finally saying what one held back, with firm resolve.

phrases.example: 시험 한 달 전부터 작심하고 공부했어요.
phrases.en: I studied with firm resolve from a month before the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작심하고 + 동사' 모양으로 열심히 하려는 각오를 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the 작심하고 + verb pattern, it adds a sense of strong determination.

phrases.en: I started exercising, but my resolve lasted only three days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음먹은 일이 사흘밖에 못 간다는 뜻으로, 결심이 약할 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a resolution lasts only three days, said often when determination is weak.
phrases.en_equiv: a resolution that lasts three days

explain_en: It feels firmer than '마음먹다', as if you have steeled yourself, and it usually appears as '작심하고 + verb'. '작심한 듯' is common when describing words or actions done with firm resolve.

t90.ax: This time I made up my mind and started a diet.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 집념 하나로 십 년 만에 꿈을 이뤘어요.
examples.en: With sheer tenacity, he achieved his dream in ten years.
That athlete's tenacity is really impressive.
The researcher kept on experimenting with tenacity.
He passed the exam through amazing persistence.

examples.ko: 집념이 지나치면 주변 사람이 힘들 수 있어요.
examples.en: If persistence goes too far, the people around you can have a hard time.
Everyone helped, moved by that determination.

explain: 한 가지 일에 오래, 끈질기게 매달리는 마음이에요. 좋게 말하면 '끈기', 지나치면 '집착'에 가까워져요. '집념이 강하다', '집념을 불태우다'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 집념이 강해서 포기하지 않아요.
phrases.en: That player has strong tenacity and doesn't give up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 끈질긴 성격을 설명할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to describe a persistent person.

phrases.en: He burned with determination to win.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 목표에 마음을 쏟는 모습을 강하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Strongly describes pouring one's heart into a goal.

phrases.en: If you study with persistence, you will surely improve.
phrases.nuance_ko: '집념'보다 쉽고 부드러운 말로, 오래 참고 해내는 힘이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer and easier than '집념'; the strength to keep going.

explain_en: It is a mind that clings to one thing for a long, stubborn time. In a good sense it is like '끈기'; when excessive it comes close to '집착'. Common patterns are '집념이 강하다' and '집념을 불태우다'.

en: to be disastrous; to be terrible

examples.ko: 시험 결과가 참담해서 말이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The exam result is so dismal that I'm speechless.

examples.ko: 참담한 소식을 듣고 모두 말을 잃었어요.
examples.en: Everyone lost their words on hearing the terrible news.
Seeing the game result, I felt devastated.
Seeing the village destroyed by the flood is heartbreaking.
He lost miserably and hung his head.

examples.ko: 지금 제 심정이 얼마나 참담한지 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: No one knows how devastated I feel right now.

explain: 결과나 소식에 크게 충격받아 마음이 괴로울 때 어울려요. '비참하다'는 처지나 모습이 불쌍할 때 더 자연스러워요. 결과, 실패, 심정, 현실 같은 말과 잘 나와요.

phrases.en: I feel devastated by the news of the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 충격으로 마음이 괴로울 때 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing when shocked and heartbroken.

phrases.en: It's hard to accept the harsh reality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받아들이기 힘들 만큼 나쁜 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a situation so bad it's hard to accept.

phrases.en: The result of that day's game was truly dismal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거의 결과나 일을 서술할 때 쓰는 해요체 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form for describing a past result or event.

explain_en: It fits when you are deeply shocked and pained by a result or news. '비참하다' is more natural when someone's situation or appearance is pitiful. It pairs well with words like results, failure, feelings and reality.
